purpose: Design of the orchestrator pattern for start-design, start-plan and start-requirements: responsibility split, context gathering, failure handling, and per-skill phases.
summary: Overview: three create skills share an orchestrator structure with common context gathering
Architecture and responsibility table across orchestrator, document search, code-collecting agent, writing, review and post-processing
Design decision: document writing runs in main context because isolated agents cannot interact with the user
Context gathering: document search via Skill tool in main context, existing code exploration via general-purpose agent
Results held in main context as search output and agent return values; no session directory
Inline prompt template for code agent with purpose, search means and output contract
Failure handling: stop and report on search failure, skipped search or agent error; zero results is valid
start-design input collection: requirements doc from context, rules via query-db-rules
start-plan phase structure and gathering matrix
start-requirements agent matrix by mode and reverse-engineering sequence
tasks: Modifying start-design, start-plan or start-requirements SKILL
Designing context gathering in create skills
Defining how orchestrators call document search SKILLs
Handling search or agent failures in orchestrated workflows
Writing prompt templates for code collection agents
